perturbation.variable: daily causal MODIS bare share of persistent row-crop land (living = 1 - bare)

uncertainty: 30 Bayesian-bootstrap refits of the median GBM over its training years (05482000: 2016-2022; 05484500: 2016-2022): each refit draws Dirichlet(1) weights per year and passes them as LightGBM row weights (no row duplication, so min_child_samples keeps counting distinct days) -> 5-95% range; plus the effect seen by the p10 and p90 quantile models; plus the conceptual reservoir model as a structurally different estimate.
flow_conditioning: All effects are changes in CONCENTRATION conditional on the observed streamflow: discharge features are model inputs and are held fixed in the counterfactual (they carry a large share of the GBM gain; see diagnostics.gain_share). Cover crops can also reduce drainage volume, so these are not load changes and a load estimate needs a separate flow assumption.
central_value_note: 'central' = the saved (deployed) models; 'bootstrap' = 30 Bayesian-bootstrap refits over training years. Both use training-period behaviour, so the effect sizes are mostly in-sample, not validated out of sample.
identification_caveat: Historical bare-share variation is overwhelmingly seasonal (bare in winter/spring, green in summer) and its year-to-year differences are driven by weather (planting/green-up timing, harvest date), not by cover-crop adoption, which stayed at single-digit % of cropland. The model therefore never saw a watershed with much more winter living cover, so the learned sensitivity is weakly identified: the monotone constraint fixes its sign (less bare soil never raises nitrate), but its size is uncertain and a 50% cut takes winter bare share far outside the training range, where trees extrapolate flat (the effect saturates). This is why the scenario engine blends it with field-trial priors.
